findings: Source lines 13–45 summarize the API flag, recurring and variable-price branches, immutability and iOS authoring correctly for the retained April guide. Add Dashboard activation, all-products eligibility and category/eligible tax-code gating, and the `2025-03-31.basil` or later API floor. The cURL examples do not include an explicit version header, so record the prose prerequisite separately. Cover server/API link creation separately from customer use of the shareable URL (old raw lines 10–35,53–123 and new raw lines 11–36,48–92).

Source lines 47–59 largely retain the correct product-specific disallowed parameter list. Preserve tax, dynamic payment methods, shipping, Connect, invoice, descriptor, consent position, limited submit-type and custom text restrictions, and describe the replace-link behavior rather than toggling the original (new raw lines 94–128 and old raw lines 125–159). Ordinary Payment Links settings do not override Managed Payments restrictions.

Source lacks the subscription consent warning, tax behavior precedence and sandbox boundaries. A Price’s explicit inclusive/exclusive setting controls tax treatment; when unspecified the documented default is tax added and the Dashboard Include tax in prices setting can change that default. Sandbox receipt emails can be sent manually but do not send automatically. Test purchases do not appear in the Link app and the guide sends readers to live-mode Checkout for the Link order-management experience. Neither link creation, test display nor returning from checkout demonstrates live payment, settlement or customer entitlement (old raw lines 161–220, new raw lines 130–189).
conflicts: Variable price limit. Mapped source lines 21 and 45 preserve the April Managed Payments guide’s explicit one-line-item rule for customer-defined prices (old raw lines 79–119). November Managed Payments prose no longer states it and only gives one Price with quantity 1 (new raw lines 64–88). The separate November general Payment Links create guide explicitly says the customer-defined Price must be the only line item with quantity 1 (raw/stripe-payment-links-create-2026-11-07.md:95-118). Keep April and separate November provenance on the rule, and link the two concepts without reading the omission as permission for multiple line items. The up-to-20 flat-rate limit is explicit in both Managed Payments captures.

Product versus general Link behavior. The generic Payment Links concept’s method override and Connect fields at wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-links.md:59–71 are general Payment Links behavior. The Managed Payments guide’s product restrictions still require removing payment_method_types and the listed Connect fields and delegate selection to Stripe’s dynamic methods (new raw lines 94–121). The Dahlia 2026-08-26 changelog permits ordinary Payment Link Connect configuration updates for future Checkout Sessions, with existing active Sessions unaffected (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-08-26-adds-connect-parameters-to-the-payment-link-update-method-2026-11-07.md:5-23). Those changes do not enable Connect for Managed Payments or make Managed Payments on a link editable (new raw lines 123–128, raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-eligibility-2026-11-07.md:9-20). Both concept routes should signal mode and object scope.

Customer authorization and identity. Mapped source lines 37–45 mention recurring price and immutability but omit that authorization obtained from a Managed Payments subscription is limited to charges by Managed Payments and separate consent is needed for outside transactions (old raw lines 173–197, new raw lines 142–166). Put this restriction on the source and reciprocal Managed Payments/Payment Links routes. Link is the buyer-facing merchant of record and order/support surface of the Stripe Managed Payments flow (raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-how-it-works-2026-11-07.md:9-29,63-83); a Payment Link’s object setting, resulting Checkout Session or Subscription, payment result and consent scope are distinct. The iOS Stripe app instruction restricts authoring a Managed Payments Payment Link. It does not prohibit a customer opening a link from an app (new raw lines 18–26,90–92).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-use-payment-links-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-managed-payments-payment-links-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-payment-links.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/use-payment-links`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/use-payment-links, new raw lines 5-36 document prior Dashboard activation, eligibility for every digital product, eligible tax codes, web Dashboard creation and the Payment Links API floor of 2025-03-31.basil. The seller creates the Payment Link with managed_payments[enabled] and line-item Prices and quantities. A recurring Price selects the subscription path. Optional subscription_data configures that subscription, including a trial, and requires at least one recurring line item. A custom_unit_amount Price lets the customer choose what to pay (new raw lines 48-92 and raw/stripe-api-payment-link-create-2026-11-07.md:270-271). The shareable link opens Checkout. Checkout Sessions, PaymentIntents, Invoices and Subscriptions are separate downstream objects that may result as applicable, including a Subscription when purchased (raw/stripe-api-payment-link-create-2026-11-07.md:151-155 and new raw lines 142-166). Stripe exercises merchant-of-record control over checkout settings, and customers see Link at checkout and for subscription or transaction support (new raw lines 94-121 and new raw lines 175-181). The link’s Managed Payments state is fixed at creation. Subscription authorization covers Managed Payments charges and separate customer consent is needed to charge outside this flow (new raw lines 123-128 and new raw lines 154-156). Checkout Session completion or a return to the site can precede delayed payment success. Use the applicable server-side webhook outcome for fulfillment. Neither the link, the return nor the sandbox view proves eligibility, capture or settlement (raw/stripe-payment-links-post-payment-2026-11-07.md:19-25 and raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-set-up-2026-11-07.md:398-408). April documents the same core flow and states the one-line-item variable-price limit explicitly (old raw lines 10-77, old raw lines 79-119, old raw lines 125-159, old raw lines 173-204). source-stripe-managed-payments-payment-links.md captures the flag, modes and restrictions but omits the creation gates, version and consent boundary.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/use-payment-links, the matched November guide retains the creation, subscription, eligibility, no-Connect, immutable-state, authorization and tax behavior of the April guide. Numbering, table alignment, API link paths and Node-to-cURL examples are presentation changes. November removes the explicit sentence about one customer-defined line item but still shows one Price and quantity 1 (old raw lines 79-119, new raw lines 64-88). Keep the dated April clause and the November general Payment Links create guide’s explicit sole-line/quantity-1 limit (raw/stripe-payment-links-create-2026-11-07.md:95-114). Preserve the 20-item flat-rate cap, the API version floor, the web Dashboard authoring restriction, the buyer consent boundary and the sandbox limitations (old raw lines 17-77, old raw lines 173-220, new raw lines 18-62, new raw lines 130-189). Add reciprocal warnings to source-stripe-managed-payments-payment-links.md and its Managed Payments and Payment Links concept routes. General Payment Links’ versioned Connect updates apply to future Checkout Sessions while Managed Payments still excludes Connect, removes manual payment_method_types and requires a new link to change its state. Both guides say that explicit Price tax_behavior controls inclusive or exclusive pricing. If unspecified, tax is added by default, and the Dashboard Include tax in prices setting can change that default (old raw lines 214-220 and new raw lines 183-189). Price tax behavior is separate from the unavailable automatic_tax and tax_id_collection Payment Link controls (new raw lines 104-105). A shared link, a browser return or a subscription/test receipt alone establishes neither live payment, settlement nor wider payment-method authorization (old raw lines 125-159, new raw lines 94-128, new raw lines 142-189).
